exposure: Combined pharmacological and surgical approach (methotrexate + hysteroscopic evacuation) with adjunct letrozole (5 mg orally for 10 days)
Combined pharmacological and surgical approach (methotrexate + hysteroscopic evacuation) without adjunct letrozole
outcome: Treatment outcomes of cesarean scar pregnancy
Biochemical indicators of efficacy (serum b-human chorionic gonadotropin, hemoglobin, renal and liver parameters)
Complications (postoperative hemoglobin reduction, red blood cell concentrate units transfused, uterine tamponade, uterine perforation or hemorrhage)
cohort: The study included 28 women diagnosed with cesarean scar pregnancy, with 16 receiving adjunct letrozole and 12 receiving only methotrexate.
finding: The incorporation of letrozole into the combined pharmacological and surgical treatment regimen for cesarean scar pregnancy did not significantly improve treatment outcomes or reduce complications.
